title: How SBOM Scope and Component Identity Affect Release Risk Decisions in npm Projects
content: Software bills of materials (SBOMs) can drive advisory triage and release decisions. We examined whether agreement among SBOM generators also indicates agreement with a deployment reference. Three generators at two sets of versions produced 504 CycloneDX SBOMs from 42 public npm repositories at fixed commits (12 pilot and 30 extension projects). We applied a common policy to a frozen npm advisory snapshot and used lockfile trees and 36 observed Linux production installations as separate references. In each version set, tools disagreed on release decisions for 17 of 30 extension projects under the study’s defaults. Disagreement fell to 0 when all tools included development dependencies. After checking both declared roots, all three generators agreed on non-development release decisions across the 36 installations. In both version sets they issued one shared BLOCK where the installed inventory gave PASS. In a separate project, one generator omitted a HIGH advisory for an installed optional package while retaining the same BLOCK decision as the installed reference. The study covers single-root npm projects and one Linux installation setting with lifecycle scripts disabled. These results support checking advisory queues and deployment decisions against the package inventory relevant to each release policy.
